deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page): Riemann is treating the minimal surface bounded by two rectilinear polygons A_1..A_n and A'_1..A'_m lying in parallel planes. The surface is doubly connected. It is mapped conformally onto half (T') of a two-sheeted Riemann surface T over the t-plane. T has branch points t = ±i and t = ±i/κ, with Δ(t) = sqrt((1+t^2)(1+κ^2 t^2)). This is an elliptic curve. Here η is the stereographic image of the surface normal (Gauss map). By the reflection principle, d log η/dt is single-valued on T and hence rational in t and Δ(t). Its zeros are at the images a, a' of the vertices and its poles at b, b'.

This page:
(1) Normalisation. One of the points a, a', b, b' may be chosen arbitrarily. This uses up the one-parameter conformal symmetry of the annulus (my interpretation). The additive constant in log η is fixed by prescribing the value η_0 of η at one vertex point a_1. Integrating then gives
log η − log η_0 = ∫_a^t φ(t,Δ(t)) dt / Δ(t).

(2) Constant count. Once a and η_0 are fixed, the expression still contains 2n+2m undetermined constants. The marginal tally reads:
- the positions a, b (n each) and a', b' (m each);
- one point is arbitrary and one is 'vollständig bestimmt' (presumably by the zero/pole balance or Abel condition for φ on the elliptic curve; my reading), leaving 2m+2n−2 free positions;
- the modulus κ^2: 1;
- the real constant factor of φ: 1.
This totals 2m+2n, or 2m+2n+1 if η_0 is included.

(3) Conditions on these constants:
- 2n+2m−2 conditions saying that the points a, a' correspond to the vertices A, A' (values of η prescribed by the edge directions);
- 2 period conditions: the real part of ∫ φ dt/Δ over a closed loop enclosing both branch points i and i/κ must vanish on both sheets. This makes |η| single-valued around the annulus.

A marginal note says that of these two conditions only one is needed, 'the other is automatically satisfied'. Riemann concludes that the number of undetermined constants equals the number of conditions imposed by the mapping problem.

(4) Second step. Place the x-axis perpendicular to the two boundary planes. Cut the surface by a cut joining the two boundary components, so that it becomes simply connected. Consider the map of the surface to the plane of the complex variable X = x + i x*, where x* is the harmonic conjugate of x. This works because the coordinate x is harmonic on a minimal surface (the transcription's 'T' is X).
- The real part x is constant on each boundary and on every section of the surface parallel to them.
- The imaginary part increases by a finite period on going around once along such a section (continued on the next page).

The next page concludes that the image is a parallelogram-like region with two sides parallel to the imaginary axis. The map is X = iC ∫ dt/Δ + C', with h = 2C ∫_0^i i dt/Δ.
errors: Constant count: the text counts 2n+2m unknowns against 2n+2m−2 + 2 conditions. The marginal remark that one of the two period conditions is automatically satisfied would make the conditions 2n+2m−1, so the bookkeeping is loose. The surplus may be absorbed by η_0 (the margin's 2m+2n+1) or by one-sheet/other-sheet symmetry. It is a heuristic constant count, not a proof of solvability.
Interpretation, not a slip by Riemann: the 2n+2m−2 vertex conditions are stated without justification of why each vertex contributes the stated number of real conditions.
No mathematical slip is visible in the displayed formula itself; it is the integrated form of the previous page's d log η/dt = φ/Δ.

results.what: Gauss map (log η) of a minimal surface bounded by two polygons in parallel planes expressed as an abelian (elliptic) integral ∫ φ(t,Δ) dt/Δ on the elliptic curve Δ^2=(1+t^2)(1+κ^2 t^2)
results.modern_name: Weierstrass–Enneper representation / Schwarz–Christoffel-type solution of Plateau's problem for polygonal boundaries, doubly connected case
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous paper ed. Hattendorff 1867); Weierstrass 1866; Schwarz for polygonal Plateau problems

results.what: Counting of free parameters (accessory parameters, modulus, factor) versus conditions (vertex correspondence, period conditions)
results.modern_name: Accessory-parameter / period-condition count (moduli count) for the Plateau–Riemann problem
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1867 posthumous); later Schwarz, Garnier (1928), Douglas

results.what: Using the coordinate x perpendicular to the boundary planes as a harmonic function, constant on the boundaries, with its conjugate having a period; mapping the cut annulus to a parallelogram via an elliptic integral of the first kind
results.modern_name: Conformal modulus of a doubly connected minimal surface via the height function (harmonic measure / flux)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Hattendorff ed. 1867, the case of boundaries in parallel planes, including two circles giving Riemann's minimal surface)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material that appears in Riemann's posthumously published minimal-surface paper (Hattendorff 1867): the reflection-principle argument, the elliptic-integral representation, the constant count, and the height-function map to a parallelogram. The only extra detail is a marginal constant tally.

checkable.asserts: The marginal tally (2m+2n−2 point positions + κ^2 + factor of φ) equals the 2n+2m unknowns stated in the text; the result is 0.
Δ(t)^2 is real for real t, which underlies the reality of the integrand on the boundary (real t-axis); the result is 0.
With t=i s, the integrand i dt/Δ(t) equals −ds/sqrt((1−s^2)(1−k^2 s^2)), so ∫_0^i i dt/Δ = −K(k) (complete elliptic integral) for 0<s<1; this is the next page's h-formula. The result is 0.
Numerical check that the period integral is the complete elliptic integral K with parameter k^2; the result is ≈ 0.

transcription_corrections: The displayed integral's denominator in the image is √(1+t^2 · 1+κ^2 t^2) = Δ(t), consistent with the previous page, not √(t(1−t)(1−k^2 t)).
The branch points enclosed by the closed loop are i and i/κ, not 1 and 1/k^2.
Line 1: 'kann auch, wie oben bemerkt, einer beliebig angenommen werden' — the interlinear 'einer' replaces 'je'.
'die zu log η hinzutretende additive Constante' — it is log η, not log q.
'Der reelle Theil des Integrals … für beide Blätter den Werth 0 haben soll' — the reading 0 is likely correct.
In the final paragraph the complex variable is X (as on the next page), not T: 'die Abbildung der Minimalfläche in der Ebene der complexen Variablen X'.
The margin reads: 'n | a, b ; m | a', b' } 1 a beliebig, 1 vollständig bestimmt; 2m+2n−2; κ^2 1; Factor von φ 1; [sum] 2m+2n; η_0 … 2m+2n+1'.
